concepts.headline: The Other Guys vs. Ortho Stretch
concepts.primary_text: Running shoes are built for a 45-minute jog. They were never designed for a 12-hour shift on hospital concrete. By hour six, that narrow toe box is squeezing your bunions. By hour nine, the thin foam has completely flattened under your heels. And by 7 PM, your feet are throbbing so hard you can barely walk to your car. That is why so many nurses switched to the Ortho Stretch Cushion Shoe. Instead of pinching your forefoot, the wide toe box lets your toes spread out naturally. Instead of flimsy foam, you get built-in anatomical arch support and a cushioned heel designed for long hours on hard floors. The stretch-knit upper breathes and expands when your feet swell in the afternoon. And the elastic no-tie laces mean you never have to bend down to re-tie them with dirty gloves. Right now for Black Friday, take 60% OFF SITEWIDE with free shipping & returns. Wear them on your next shift with our 30-day wear test trial. If your feet do not feel the difference, return them within 30 days for a full refund.

Her heels are burning. Her toes feel crushed inside standard athletic sneakers that lost their cushion by noon. She has to peel her shoes off before she can even start the engine. The second nurse walks straight to her car without limping. She is wearing the Ortho Stretch Cushion Shoe. The anatomical arch support kept her arches from collapsing under her body weight. The cushioned heel absorbed every hard strike on rock-hard hospital linoleum. And the wide toe box gave her toes room to spread without rubbing against stiff seams. Both worked the same grueling shift. Only one gets to go home without throbbing feet. Try a pair for 30 days and feel the difference on your next shift.

concepts.headline: 8 fixes to survive one 12. Really?
on_image_text: Or just one pair of shoes built for 12 hours on hard floors.
concepts.primary_text: Look inside the tote bag of any nurse working a 12-hour shift. You will find thick gel insoles stuffed into running shoes. Graduated compression socks pulled up tight. A frozen water bottle waiting in the breakroom freezer. A blister kit, arch wrap tape, and two ibuprofen tucked into a scrub pocket just in case. You are stacking six different bandaids because your sneakers were never built for hospital floors. Standard running shoes are designed for light jogging on a track. They taper in at the toes, cramp your bunions, and lose their cushioning three hours into your shift. The Ortho Stretch Cushion Shoe replaces that entire survival kit with one pair of shoes. The wide toe box gives your toes room to spread without chafing or blistering. The anatomical arch support stops your arches from flattening under your body weight. And the thick cushioned heel absorbs every hard step on unforgiving linoleum. Put them on for your next shift with our 30-day wear test trial. See how many fixes you can leave at home.
